text: Good morning, Your Honors, and may it please the court. My name is Michelle Esparza, counsel for the appellant, Eduardo Fuentes. My co-counsel, David Miraso, will be arguing the 10 minutes allotted to the appellant for rebuttal. I will be addressing why the trial court abused its discretion when it denied Eduardo's application for temporary injunction, even though he pleaded and proved every element necessary to establish his right to a temporary injunction. Today, I will be discussing the following four important points. First, the trial court changed the status quo when it granted Sessax Ex Parte TRO three years into an ongoing lawsuit without a hearing, without due process, without notice. Second, the 2013 stock transfers are void, ad initio, from the beginning because transfers of Fox holding company stock by gift is prohibited under the shareholder's agreement. Third, the April 2019 actions taken by Cesar Enyamel to Alistair Eduardo as president of TIGO are void and of no effect because they were taken without a quorum in violation of Fox holding company's governing documents. Fourth and finally, Eduardo pleaded and proved that he and TIGO suffered irreparable, probable, and imminent harm because he has been deprived of his position as president of TIGO and his rights as a shareholder and director of FHC, Fox holding company. TIGO is also being controlled by two persons that have not been duly elected officers, and that continue to operate Fox holding and TIGO in violation of the governing documents of both corporations and in violation of the Railroad Commission safety rules. The Texas Supreme Court said that the very purpose of an injunction is to preserve the status quo of the litigation subject matter pending a trial on the merits. The Texas Supreme Court has defined the status quo to mean the last actual, peaceable, non-contested status which preceded the pending controversy. Here, the last actual, peaceable, non-contested status which preceded the pending controversy was the status of the parties at the inception of the suit in 2016 up to April 2019, which was Eduardo serving as TIGO's duly elected president. It cannot be that the judicial removal of a company's president three years into a lawsuit, which resulted in two companies being operated every single day in violation of their own governing documents by two people that have not been rightfully elected officers of the company is the actual, peaceable, non-contested status. All Eduardo's request for temporary injunction asked for is that the trial court restore the status quo, but it abused its discretion when in the face of clear, key, undisputed facts and a set of governing documents that are clear on their face and must be construed as written. It wrongfully denied Eduardo's temporary injunction by applying the law incorrectly to the facts. The facts necessary for the resolution of this appeal and for the determination of Eduardo's request for injunction are not disputed. It is undisputed that the articles of incorporation, the bylaws, and shareholders agreement, which are in the appendix of the appellant's brief, are the governing documents of Fox Holding Company. It is also undisputed that in April 2019, Cesar Enamel acting alone took a series of corporate actions on behalf of Fox Holding Company and TIGO in an attempt to oust Eduardo as TIGO's president. We do dispute at the trial court level, that the 2013 transfers ever occurred. But for the purposes of this appeal, we are assuming that they did occur because we argue that even if they did, Eduardo should still prevail. Cesar Enamel's purported April 2019 actions removing Eduardo as TIGO's president are void for many reasons. But first, because the 2013 stock gifts are void ab initio under the clear and unambiguous expressed terms of the shareholders agreement. Cesar Enamel claimed that they had the authority to take the April 2019 corporate actions to oust Eduardo because in 2013, their father, Mr. Fuentes Varela, allegedly gifted CAFSA's interest in Fox Holding to himself, then in turn gifted that interest in equal shares to his four children. Supposedly giving Cesar Enamel together a majority interest in Fox Holding Company. However, the Fox Holding Company shareholders agreement does not permit the exact type of gift transfers they allege occurred in 2013. The shareholders agreement is unambiguous, is clear, is dispositive. It should be enforced as written, and it says the following. Rule number one, transfers are not permitted, except as expressly authorized in this agreement. Rule number two, if a transfer that is not authorized by this agreement is attempted, it is void ab initio, as though it never happened. So what is a transfer of shares permitted under the shareholders agreement? There is only one permissible transfer of shares under the shareholders agreement.
